data.text: I just got a tentative slot. Direct cardioversion is being held for Wednesday, March 11 at 10:20 AM with 8:50 AM arrival in the cardiac procedures unit.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Is cardioversion still the plan, or are we trying to just slow the rate?

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Cardioversion is still the plan. Based on what we know so far, we were aiming for Wednesday morning, but I want the lab results and the medication history fully reconciled first.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Until then, continue apixaban 5 milligrams twice daily without interruption. Increase metoprolol tartrate from 25 milligrams twice daily to 37.5 milligrams twice daily starting tonight.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Use acetaminophen instead if needed, and start magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights because your previous magnesium trend has been low-normal.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Keep lisinopril 10 milligrams daily for now, but hold the morning dose on the day of the procedure once the date is finalized.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: So right now I keep taking apixaban, I raise the metoprolol tonight, I stop ibuprofen, and I begin the magnesium tonight?

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Correct. Also do not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion.

prior_context.speaker: agent_memcare
prior_context.text: Cardiology plan update: continue apixaban 5 mg BID without interruption, increase metoprolol tartrate to 37.5 mg BID starting tonight, stop ibuprofen/NSAIDs, use acetaminophen if needed, start magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights, continue lisinopril 10 mg daily but hold morning dose on procedure day.

prior_context.speaker: labtech_mira
prior_context.text: Your labs are back: hemoglobin 14.1, potassium 4.1, magnesium 1.7, creatinine 1.0, and TSH 1.9.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Those labs are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, and the magnesium result supports the supplement plan we just discussed.

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
